name: Tawang Monastery (Gaden Namgyal Lhatse)
description: Largest Buddhist monastery in India and second-largest in the world, founded in 1680-81 by Merak Lama Lodre Gyatso under the guidance of the 5th Dalai Lama. Perched on a ridge overlooking the Tawang Chu valley at about 3000 m.
facts: Founded 1680-81 by Merak Lama Lodre Gyatso
Home to hundreds of monks and a large Buddha statue
Birthplace connection to 6th Dalai Lama nearby

name: Sela Pass
description: High-altitude mountain pass at 4170 m on the border of Tawang and West Kameng districts. Gateway to Tawang on NH-13, with Sela Lake nearby; often snow-covered. Sela Tunnel provides all-weather access below the pass.
facts: On border of Tawang and West Kameng districts
Sela Tunnel opened for year-round connectivity

name: Sangetsar Tso (Madhuri Lake)
description: High-altitude lake formed by an earthquake, popularly known as Madhuri Lake after a Bollywood song sequence filmed here. Features submerged tree trunks and scenic mountain backdrop on the route toward Bum La.
facts: Formed by earthquake with standing dead trees
On the road to Bum La Pass

name: Nuranang Falls (Jang Falls)
description: Spectacular 100 m high waterfall near Jang town, originating from slopes of Sela Pass. Popular stop on the route to Tawang with nearby hydel plant and scenic valley views.
facts: Also called Bong Bong or Jung Falls
Near Jang town about 40 km from Tawang
Song sequence from Koyla filmed nearby

name: Bum La Pass
description: High-altitude border pass at about 4600 m on the Indo-China frontier, 37 km from Tawang. Requires special permit; historically significant and offers stark Himalayan views. Border Personnel Meeting point.
facts: Historical trade route and 1962 war site

name: Urgelling Monastery
description: Historic Buddhist monastery and birthplace of the 6th Dalai Lama Tsangyang Gyatso (born 1683). Smaller and quieter than Tawang Monastery, located near Tawang town.

name: Tawang War Memorial
description: 40-foot-high stupa-style memorial dedicated to Indian soldiers who lost their lives in the 1962 Sino-Indian War. Features light and sound show and overlooks the Tawang valley.
facts: Light and sound show in evenings

name: Jaswant Garh War Memorial
description: Memorial honoring Rifleman Jaswant Singh Rawat of 4 Garhwal Rifles for his bravery in the 1962 war near Nuranang. Maintained by Indian Army; includes bunker and exhibits. On the main highway to Tawang.
facts: Dedicated to Rifleman Jaswant Singh Rawat (MVC)
Near Nuranang/Sela route about 25-40 km from Tawang

name: Pankang Teng Tso (PT Tso)
description: Pristine high-altitude lake about 17 km from Tawang, surrounded by rhododendrons and mountains. Freezes in winter; popular for scenic views and photography.
facts: Also called Panga Teng Tso or PTSO

name: Tawang Town
description: District headquarters and main tourist base in Tawang district at about 3000 m elevation. Gateway to monasteries, lakes, and high-altitude sites; Monpa culture and markets.

name: Zemithang
description: Remote border village and circle HQ in western Tawang district on the Nyamjang Chu river. First point where the 14th Dalai Lama entered India in 1959; near Gorsam Chorten and Bhutan border.
facts: Dalai Lama's first entry point into India in 1959
Border area with Tibet and Bhutan

name: Chakzam Iron Bridge
description: Ancient 15th-century iron chain suspension bridge across the Tawang Chu River, built by Tibetan engineer Thangtong Gyalpo. Historic architectural marvel near Tawang.
facts: Built in 15th century by Thangtong Gyalpo
One of few surviving examples of its kind
